20261122-chemistry-e1-2.s.s1.hint.1: Coating the surface can block oxygen and water.

20261122-chemistry-e2-2.title: Even if water and cooking oil
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.topic: Even if water and cooking oil
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.goal: Apply principles of Even if water and cooking oil to solve the reasoning problem.
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.material: Even if water and cooking oil are put in one bottle and shaken hard, they separate completely into two layers again after sitting still for a moment. Why?
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.thinking.0: Even if water and cooking oil
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.prompt: Even if water and cooking oil are put in one bottle and shaken hard, they separate completely into two layers again after sitting still for a moment. Why?
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.explain: Water is a polar molecule and cooking oil is a nonpolar molecule, so they do not mix, and the density of cooking oil (about 0.92 g/cm³) is lower than that of water (1.0 g/cm³), so it rises to the upper layer.
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.hint.0: Water is polar and oil is nonpolar, so they do not dissolve in each other.
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.hint.1: Oil is lighter than water (less dense), so it floats on top.
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o0: Because cooking oil does not mix with water and is less dense than water, so it floats on top
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o1: Because the cooking oil absorbs the water
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o2: Because the water is warmer than the cooking oil
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o3: Because the cooking oil has hardened into a solid
